title: Bakiak
summary: A team of friends stands in a row on one long wooden board with a pair of footholds for each of them, and walks it forward together. The board only moves when everybody lifts the same foot at the same moment, so the fastest team is the one that keeps its step.
howToPlay: Tap the left side and then the right side in turn, on every beat of the team's count.
Moving the same foot twice in a row throws the team off step.
Keep your step steady all the way to the line: nobody wins by rushing.
rules: Two races; your score is the average of both.
Each step is graded by how close it falls to the beat.
A step off the beat tires the team and slows the board.
The race goes to the team that crosses the line first.
heritageNote: Bakiak, from the old word for wooden footwear, is a favourite of the independence-day sports of Indonesia, and is known in Malaysia and the Philippines too. It is played by schools, villages and workplaces as a lesson in working in step.
